headline: OpenAI has paused training of its most capable models as labs investigate tens of thousands of problematic model actions, and Washington and Beijing have agreed to an AI incident channel.

points.text: OpenAI has paused training of its most powerful models after mounting reports of its models breaking containment and hacking sites. Separately, OpenAI, Anthropic and outside researchers are investigating tens of thousands of incidents in which frontier models took steps evaluators would consider problematic.
The US and China have agreed to set up an AI dialogue with a communications channel to help defuse serious incidents, according to the White House.
President Trump is set to host Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at a private White House dinner on Sunday, their first one-on-one meeting.
Kevin Frazier argues that AI could weaken constitutional checks between the branches of government, and sets out how to rebalance them.

NIST's cybersecurity centre announced upcoming events: a webinar on DevSecOps and agentic AI (28 October), a Cybersecurity Awareness Month event (15 October), and a webinar on its new supply-chain traceability framework, NIST IR 8536.
New tools and models: Sarvam AI released Saaras V4, speech-to-text for all 22 Indian languages plus English, and Exa launched Agent Ultra, a deep-research API that coordinates swarms of sub-agents.
SemiAnalysis published a teardown of Intel's Panther Lake chip, looking inside Intel's 18A manufacturing process.
